notes.meaning: In the third year of King Cyrus of Persia, God gave Daniel an important message about a great coming conflict and hardship. Daniel was now an elderly man, yet God gave him understanding so he could grasp the true meaning of the vision. God reveals his dependable plans to his people even during times of political unrest.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars think chapters 10–12 were written after the events they describe, in the second century BC. Daniel 11 is so detailed that they treat it as history, not prediction.

notes.meaning: Daniel spent three full weeks in deep sorrow and prayer. He mourned because the exiles who had returned to Jerusalem faced severe opposition while trying to rebuild the temple, and many other Jews remained scattered in Babylon. God's servants naturally share in the griefs and struggles of God's people.

During these three weeks, Daniel chose to eat only plain, simple food, giving up meat and wine. He also stopped using fragrant olive oil on his skin, which was a common custom during times of joy and celebration. This humble self-denial helped him give his whole heart to serious prayer.

On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, Daniel was standing along the bank of the great Tigris River. His three weeks of fasting had just ended right after the Passover season. God chose this quiet riverbank outside the capital to reveal himself to his faithful servant.

Daniel looked up and saw an awe-inspiring figure dressed in fine linen, wearing a belt of pure gold around his waist. The clean linen resembled the sacred garments worn by Israel's priests, showing great purity and holiness. The shining gold showed royal authority and heavenly majesty.

differ.view: This is a great angel in human form, sent from heaven. The details are meant to show he is no ordinary man, not to picture Christ's priesthood.

notes.meaning: The figure's body sparkled like a brilliant jewel, his face flashed like lightning, and his eyes blazed like fiery torches. His arms and legs gleamed like polished bronze, and his voice thundered with the sound of a massive crowd. This dazzling sight revealed the holy power and terrifying majesty of heaven.

differ.view: This is a great angel in human form, sent from heaven. The details are meant to show he is no ordinary man, not to picture Christ's priesthood.

notes.meaning: Only Daniel saw this heavenly vision. The men who were with him saw nothing, yet a sudden, overwhelming dread seized them, causing them to run away and hide. God can make his terrifying presence felt even by people whose eyes are kept from seeing it.

Daniel was left entirely alone, staring at this immense and magnificent vision. The sheer glory drained away all his physical strength, leaving his face deathly pale and completely helpless. When mortal beings encounter the holy majesty of God, even the strongest person feels totally powerless.

As Daniel listened to the voice of the heavenly figure, he was overwhelmed by what he heard. He collapsed into a deep swoon, lying flat on the earth with his face pressed to the ground. Experiencing the majesty of heaven brings human beings into utter humility before God.

A hand reached out and touched Daniel, lifting him up so that he was shaking on his hands and knees. He was still far too weak and frightened to stand on his own two feet. God gently raises up his fallen servants one step at a time when they are overwhelmed.

The messenger called Daniel a person deeply loved and highly valued by God. He told Daniel to pay close attention to his words and instructed him to stand upright. Daniel rose to his feet, still shaking with awe at the glory of God's messenger.

The messenger told Daniel not to be afraid, assuring him that God had heard his prayers from the very first day he began to humble himself and seek understanding. The angel had been sent out immediately in direct response to those prayers. God hears the cries of his humble people without any delay.

The messenger explained that an evil spiritual power, the prince of Persia, had opposed him for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of God's chief angelic leaders who protects Israel, came to help him in the unseen struggle. Real spiritual conflicts take place behind the scenes of human history, but God's side always wins.

differ.view: The "prince of Persia" was the Persian king Cambyses, who blocked the building of the temple. God's angel worked against him to stop him harming the Jews even more.
Michael is not a created angel but Christ himself, the head of the angels.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some teach that certain evil spirits rule over places, and that believers should pray against them by name to break their hold. Others answer that Daniel did not even know about this battle.

notes.meaning: The messenger came to explain what would happen to the Jewish people in the distant future. The vision pointed ahead through long years of trial until the end times. God comforts his people by showing that the future is securely in his hands.

differ.view: "The latter days" point mainly to the future of the nation of Israel at the end of this age, before Christ returns. The church does not replace Israel in this promise.

notes.meaning: As the angel spoke about these heavy future events, Daniel lowered his eyes toward the ground in deep reverence and found himself unable to speak. The sheer weight and wonder of what he was hearing completely stunned him. God's great revelations naturally fill human hearts with silent awe.

A heavenly figure appearing in human form reached out and touched Daniel's lips, restoring his ability to talk. Daniel confessed that the terrifying vision had filled him with sharp distress and drained away all his strength. God provides the help his people need so they can speak and pour out their struggles to him.

Daniel wondered how a frail, mortal servant like himself could possibly speak with such a glorious heavenly lord. He felt breathless, terrified, and emptied of all power. When people catch a glimpse of heavenly glory, they quickly recognize their own human frailty.

The heavenly figure touched Daniel a second time, restoring his physical vigor and lifting his spirits. Daniel could not bear to receive God's message without this divine assistance. God faithfully strengthens his servants whenever their calling feels too heavy to carry alone.

The messenger comforted Daniel again by reminding him that God loved him dearly, telling him to be at peace and to be courageous. As soon as these words were spoken, Daniel felt strength flood into his body and asked the messenger to speak. God's comforting word brings calm and courage to weary hearts.

The angel asked Daniel if he understood why he had come, and then explained that he had to return to fight the evil spiritual prince of Persia. After that conflict, the spirit prince of Greece would rise to influence world affairs. God's heavenly messengers actively oppose dark spiritual forces to protect God's purpose for his people.

differ.view: The fight is against the human kings of Persia. God would hold back their cruelty, and later Alexander's, to protect his people.

notes.meaning: The angel promised to reveal what is written in God's Book of Truth, which contains God's sovereign and unchangeable plan for history. He noted that only Michael, the angelic guardian of Daniel's people, stood beside him in this spiritual battle. Believers can have peace knowing that God's eternal plans can never be broken by any earthly or demonic power.

differ.view: "Michael your prince" is Christ, the true protector and head of his people.
